subject: Post-call: Acme discovery + competitive/obs tooling test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed test plan (competitive + observability)

Hi Lisa  thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the evaluation run: 

Call highlights:
- Primary P1: reduce inference tail latency for user-facing chat and keep token costs within our target.
- P2: stronger observability (per-route latency/cost, token-level breakdowns, and tracing for request flows).
- You mentioned prior tests with AWS Bedrock and Vertex and that you saw inconsistent KV-cache behavior on long sessions.

What we propose for the next tests (simple, reproducible):
1) Latency & throughput: 1k concurrent chat sessions with synthetic prompt mix (we'll use your sample prompt set). Measure p50/p95/p99 and per-token compute cost against the same model family.
2) Long-tail / KV cache behavior: 100 sessions with long histories (8k+ tokens), measure steady-state latency and memory growth.
3) Observability smoke: verify per-route dashboards (latency, tokens, cost), OpenTelemetry traces attached to requests, and log retention/exports.
4) Failure/reliability: simulated node loss and model fallback to ensure graceful degradation.

Deliverables from Redwood: a test harness (JMeter + simple client), a test plan spreadsheet, and an observability checklist. Attached: redwood-test-plan.xlsx and redwood-observability-cheatsheet.pdf.

Ask from Acme: a small sample dataset (10-20 representative prompts) and temporary S3 access or a signed URL for the harness. Also would be helpful to confirm which hyperscaler setups you ran (Bedrock/Vertex) and any config notes (batching settings, sequence length).

Next steps / timeline:
- Today/Friday: you share sample prompts + S3 access (or we can use the sample link you suggested).
- Monday: Michael will spin up the test harness and propose exact test times/windows.
- Test week: run tests and deliver a comparison report + dashboards.

Looping in Michael (SE) and Dev (infra) to coordinate the test infra and timing. If this looks good I'll drop the HubSpot mutual action plan and propose calendar windows.

Thanks 
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (650) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-test-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-observability-cheatsheet.pdf (pdf)

From: Lisa Huang <lisa@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed test plan (competitive + observability)

Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few quick answers: 

- I'll share a small prompt set and a signed URL to an S3 bucket with sample documents by EOD tomorrow.
- We ran initial evaluation tests against Bedrock (stringer config) and Vertex AI endpoints. Bedrock had higher p95 in our burst tests; Vertex seemed cheaper per-token but we lost some telemetry fidelity.
- Our main concern is the long chat sessions  we saw latency spikes past 2 seconds on p95 when histories grew.

One ask: can you show how Redwood's per-route cost attribution would look for a mixed workload (chat + embeddings + reranking)? We need the billing transparency to push this through procurement.

Looping in our evaluation mailing list so the rest of the team sees the plan: ai-eval@acmecorp.com

Thanks 
Lisa Huang
Senior Product Manager, AI Platforms
Acme Corp
lisa@acmecorp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed test plan (competitive + observability)

Thanks Lisa  appreciate the context. 

Michael  can you take point on the test harness and draft an exact test matrix for the items below? Key outputs we want in the matrix: test name, workload profile, expected metric outputs (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost/token estimate), and how to reproduce. Also include the observability checks: OpenTelemetry traces per request, per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and export to S3/BigQuery.

Dev  we'll need some short-lived infra for the harness (k8s worker + S3 capture)  can you sketch an approximate infra cost and access requirements?

From Marissa to Acme: once we have the matrix I'll propose 2x 4-hour windows next week for the canary runs and a longer 24-hour run to validate steady-state behavior.

Thanks 
Marissa

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lisa Huang <lisa@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed test plan (competitive + observability)

Thanks  I'll take point. High level plan below; I'll drop a detailed test matrix in HubSpot and share the exact runbook by Monday morning.

Planned quick test matrix (summary):
- Latency/throughput: 3 workloads (chat-light, chat-heavy, embeddings-batch). 2x 4-hour windows (canary) + 24-hour steady-state run. Measure p50/p95/p99 and cost/token.
- KV/long sessions: 100 sessions with 8k+ token histories, check p95 growth and memory metrics.
- Observability: verify per-route dashboards, OpenTelemetry spans with trace IDs, token-level cost breakdown exported to S3.
- Failure scenarios: kill one GPU node during a canary window and verify fallback to a compatible model variant.

Access we need from Acme:
- Signed URL or temporary S3 creds for sample-prompt-set (10-20 prompts)
- A test account for any firewall whitelisting (IP ranges will be provided)

Tentative dates:
- Canary windows: Wed Feb 24 10:00-14:00 PST and Thu Feb 25 10:00-14:00 PST
- 24-hour steady run: Fri Feb 26 00:00-23:59 PST

I'll also include a short example dashboard link showing token-level cost per route. Will share the dashboard and runbook Monday.

 Michael Grant
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com
